newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Bucher 1996 profit jumps, sees 1997 rise.
newsitem.headline: Bucher 1996 profit jumps, sees 1997 rise.

text.p: Bucher Holding AG said 1996 group net profit soared 37.3 percent to 49.3 million Swiss francs, but this year profits and sales were only expected to show a slight rise.

Bucher, which produces agricultural machinery, vechicles and other mechanical engineering products, also said in a letter to shareholders that it planned to cut the nominal value of its bearer shares by 20 francs and registered shares by four francs.
The capital repayment to shareholders is planned for early September.

In addition, the board of directors will ask shareholders on June 5 to approve a dividend of 12 francs per bearer shares, down from 22 francs and 2.40 francs per registered share, down from 4.40 francs.
The rise in net profit was mainly due to a 16.8 percent rise in sales to 1.120 billion francs and operational improvements.
Operating profit rose 18.8 percent to 63.2 million francs and cash flow jumped 49.3 percent to 119.7 million.
Bucher said it was not expecting any significant boost to its business this year due to the sluggish economy.
But a renewed and updated product range and a reworking of the company's operating structure should have positive effects.
"All in all we expect a slight increase in sales and in profits improvement in our core business as long as there are no unforeseen market or currency developments," Bucher said.
